title: Why Are There Lights on the Floor of Every Airplane?
description:
On the second of June, nineteen eighty-three, a burning airliner landed in Cincinnati. The doors opened, fresh air rushed in, and in about ninety seconds the cabin exploded into flames. Twenty-three people died. Almost everything you will see in this video exists because of nights like that one. Ten small things on every airliner, things you walk past without noticing, each one written into the rules by a disaster. And number five burns at more than four hundred degrees.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:38 1. The lights on the floor
3:26 2. The smoke detector in the lavatory
5:07 3. The extinguisher in the trash bin
6:47 4. The seat cushions
8:31 5. The oxygen mask
10:18 6. The seat frame
12:07 7. The escape slide
13:53 8. Arm the doors and cross check
15:09 9. The life vest
16:49 10. The cockpit door
18:28 The verdict

Sources:
- Air Canada 797 (2 June 1983): Wikipedia, "Air Canada Flight 797" (citing NTSB AAR-86/02) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Canada_Flight_797 ; NTSB report https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/AAR8602.pdf
- Floor lighting, lavatory smoke detectors, bin extinguishers, Halon, seat cushions, heat release panels, 16g seats: FAA Fact Sheet, "Aircraft Survivability" https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/2022-07/FAA-FactSheet-Aircraft-Survivability.pdf
- Dimmed cabin lights, photoluminescent strips, Flight Safety Foundation 83%: AFAR, "Why airplanes dim cabin lights for takeoff and landing" https://www.afar.com/magazine/why-airplanes-dim-cabin-lights-for-takeoff-and-landing
- Oxygen generators and ValuJet 592: Migflug, "Airplane Oxygen Masks: How Long They Last and Why They Get Hot" https://migflug.com/afterburner/airplane-oxygen-masks-chemical-generator-how-long-they-last/
- Escape slides, 90-second rule, slide-rafts: PlaneFYI, "Evacuation Slide" https://planefyi.com/glossary/evacuation-slide/
- Arming doors and cross-check: Islands, "What It Means When a Flight Attendant Performs a Cross-Check" https://www.islands.com/1943339/meaning-of-cross-check-to-flight-attendants/
- Ethiopian Airlines 961 (23 Nov 1996): Migflug, "Flight 961: The Hijacking That Ended in the Ocean" https://migflug.com/afterburner/flight-961-the-hijacking-that-ended-in-the-ocean/
- Bulletproof cockpit doors (April 2003): Lawrence Journal-World / AP, "Airlines will meet new cockpit door requirement" https://www2.ljworld.com/news/2003/apr/05/airlines_will_meet/
